#### 1. aplastic anemia  —  Tier 2 — Strong / Probable  (fitness 0.697)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5685942, Reactome:R-HSA-5693554, Reactome:R-HSA-5693568, Reactome:R-HSA-5693579, Reactome:R-HSA-912446)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in Fanconi anemia pathway genes (e.g., FANCA, BRCA2) (HGNC:9820) —DISRUPTS→ Fanconi anemia pathway (GO:0000077); Fanconi anemia pathway (GO:0000077) —LEADS_TO→ DNA repair (GO:0006281); DNA repair (GO:0006281) —LEADS_TO→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571) —LEADS_TO→ Myelodysplastic syndromes (MONDO:0013248); Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571) —LEADS_TO→ Aplastic anemia (MONDO:0015909); JAK2 (HGNC:6074) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); MPL (HGNC:7518) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); CALR (HGNC:1849) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); PIGA (HGNC:8978) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); PIGT (HGNC:9014) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571); SH2B3 (HGNC:10714) —DISRUPTS→ Hematopoiesis (GO:0007571). Loss-of-function mutations in genes within the Fanconi anemia pathway (e.g., FANCA, BRCA2) impair DNA repair, leading to genomic instability and contributing to the pathogenesis of myelodysplastic syndromes. Similarly, mutations in genes like JAK2, MPL, CALR, PIGA, PIGT, and SH2B3, which are involved in hematopoietic stem cell signaling and function, can lead to aplastic anemia. Both pathways converge on the disruption of normal hematopoiesis, resulting in the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of myelodysplastic syndromes and aplastic anemia.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the causal variants for one disease lead to gain-of-function or dominant-negative effects, while the other requires loss-of-function, would falsify this shared loss-of-function mechanism. Furthermore, identification of entirely distinct molecular pathways for each disease that do not converge on hematopoiesis would also falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in the cited genes associated with either disease would suggest alternative etiological mechanisms.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared molecular underpinnings, particularly the disruption of DNA repair and hematopoietic stem cell function, could lead to the development of targeted therapies applicable to both myelodysplastic syndromes and aplastic anemia, such as those aimed at restoring DNA repair capacity or modulating hematopoietic stem cell signaling pathways.
